recipes.title: Tuscan Lemon Chicken Piccata
recipes.description: Golden chicken cutlets in a bright lemon, garlic and caper sauce. Serve with roasted asparagus or a little angel hair pasta.
ingredients: ¼ cup fresh parsley, chopped, plus more to garnish

steps.text: Slice each breast in half horizontally to make 8 thin cutlets. Season both sides with the salt, pepper and Italian seasoning, then dredge lightly in flour, shaking off any excess.

Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the cutlets in batches, 3–4 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through (165°F inside). Move to a plate and tent loosely with foil.
Lower the heat to medium and melt the butter in the same skillet. Stir in the garlic and cook for about 30 seconds, just until fragrant.
Pour in the broth and lemon juice, scraping up the browned bits from the pan. Stir in the capers and lemon zest and simmer 3–4 minutes, until slightly reduced.
Return the chicken and any juices to the skillet and spoon the sauce over the top. Simmer for 2 minutes to warm through.
Scatter with parsley and a few extra lemon slices. Lovely with roasted asparagus, a green salad or angel hair pasta.

recipes.kitchenNote: Squeeze the lemons fresh and add a little extra zest at the very end. Leftover sauce is wonderful tossed through a bowl of buttered pasta the next day.

recipes.title: Blueberry Buttermilk Pancakes
recipes.description: Tall, tender buttermilk pancakes dotted with jammy blueberries. A slow Saturday morning on a plate.
ingredients: 3 Tbsp unsalted butter, melted, plus more for the pan

steps.text: In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda and salt.
In a second bowl, whisk the buttermilk, eggs, melted butter and vanilla until smooth.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry and fold with a spatula until just combined. A few lumps are good. Let the batter rest for 5 minutes.
Warm a griddle or large skillet over medium heat and brush it lightly with butter.
Pour ¼ cup of batter per pancake and scatter a few blueberries on top. Cook 2–3 minutes, until bubbles form and the edges look set, then flip and cook 1–2 minutes more.
Keep finished pancakes in a 200°F oven while you cook the rest. Serve with a pat of butter and warm maple syrup.

recipes.kitchenNote: Don't press the pancakes after flipping. Let them rise on their own. Frozen blueberries work too; add them straight from the freezer so they don't bleed.

recipes.title: Turkish Red Lentil Soup
recipes.description: Mercimek çorbası: a silky, golden lentil soup finished with sizzling chili-mint oil and a squeeze of lemon.

items: 1 tsp Aleppo pepper, or ½ tsp red pepper flakes

steps.text: Warm the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and carrot and cook 6–8 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft and sweet.
Stir in the garlic, tomato paste, cumin and paprika and cook for 1 minute, until the paste darkens and smells toasty.
Add the lentils and broth and bring to a boil. Lower the heat, partly cover and simmer 20–25 minutes, until the lentils have completely collapsed.
Purée with an immersion blender until smooth. Thin with a splash of hot water if it is too thick, then season with salt.
Warm the olive oil in a small pan until shimmering. Take it off the heat and stir in the Aleppo pepper and dried mint; it will sizzle and turn red.
Ladle the soup into bowls, swirl over the chili-mint oil and serve with lemon wedges for squeezing.

recipes.kitchenNote: Don't skip the lemon. It wakes the whole bowl up. The soup thickens as it sits, so loosen leftovers with a little water when you reheat them.

recipes.title: Provençal Ratatouille
recipes.description: Summer vegetables cooked one by one, then simmered together with tomato, thyme and good olive oil.
ingredients: 5 Tbsp olive oil, divided, plus more to finish
1 medium eggplant (about 1 lb), cut into ¾-inch cubes
2 medium zucchini, cut into ¾-inch half-moons
1 red and 1 yellow bell pepper, cut into 1-inch pieces
1 can (28 oz) whole peeled tomatoes, crushed by hand
1½ tsp salt, plus more to taste

steps.text: Heat 2 Tbsp of the oil in a wide, heavy pot over medium-high heat. Add the eggplant with a pinch of salt and cook 8–10 minutes, stirring, until golden. Spoon into a bowl.
Add 1 Tbsp oil and the zucchini and cook about 5 minutes, until lightly browned but still firm. Add to the eggplant.
Add the last 2 Tbsp oil, the onion and the peppers. Cook 8–10 minutes over medium heat until soft, then stir in the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and their juice, the thyme, bay leaf, salt and pepper. Simmer for 15 minutes, until slightly thickened.
Return the eggplant and zucchini to the pot, cover and simmer gently 15–20 minutes, until everything is tender but still holds its shape.
Fish out the bay leaf and thyme stems. Fold in the basil, taste for salt and finish with a thread of olive oil. Serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.kitchenNote: Ratatouille is even better the next day, so make a big pot. Spoon leftovers over polenta or toast, or bake them with eggs cracked right on top.

recipes.title: Irish Soda Bread
recipes.description: A craggy, golden loaf made with just four ingredients and no yeast. From bowl to oven in ten minutes.
ingredients: 4 cups (500 g) all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
1¾ cups (420 ml) cold buttermilk, plus a splash more if needed

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 425°F (220°C) and dust a baking sheet or cast-iron skillet with flour.
Whisk the flour, baking soda and salt together in a large bowl, then make a well in the center.
Pour in most of the buttermilk and stir with a fork or one cupped hand until a soft, shaggy dough forms. Add the rest only if dry flour remains.
Turn the dough onto a floured counter and pat it into a round about 2 inches high. Handle it as little as possible to keep the loaf tender.
Set the round on the sheet and cut a deep cross across the top with a floured knife, almost to the edges, to help it bake through.
Bake 35–40 minutes, until deep golden and hollow-sounding when tapped underneath. Cool on a rack, wrapped in a clean tea towel for a softer crust.

recipes.kitchenNote: Granny always said the cross was there to let the fairies out. It's at its best the day it's baked, still a little warm, with plenty of good salted butter.

recipes.title: Grandma's Apple Crumble
recipes.description: Soft cinnamon apples under a buttery oat crumble, baked until bubbling. Pass the custard.

items: 2½ lb tart apples (about 6), peeled, cored and sliced
½ cup (100 g) light brown sugar
½ cup (1 stick) cold unsalted butter, cubed
Custard, cream or vanilla ice cream, to serve

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 375°F (190°C) and butter a 2-quart baking dish.
In a large bowl, toss the apple slices with the sugar, lemon juice, flour and cinnamon. Tip into the dish and spread them out evenly.
Mix the flour, brown sugar, oats, cinnamon and salt. Rub in the cold butter with your fingertips until the mixture clumps like damp sand with a few larger pebbles.
Scatter the crumble loosely over the apples, right to the edges. Don't press it down; the little gaps let it crisp.
Bake 40–45 minutes, until the top is deep golden and the juices bubble thickly at the edges.
Let it settle for 10 minutes, then spoon into bowls with warm custard, cold cream or a scoop of vanilla ice cream.

recipes.kitchenNote: Use a mix of apples if you can, some sharp and some sweet. A handful of blackberries tucked in with the apples was always Grandma's late-summer secret.

recipes.title: Masala Chai
recipes.description: Strong black tea simmered with milk, fresh ginger and whole warm spices. Comfort in a cup.
ingredients: 2 tsp loose Assam tea, or 2 black tea bags

steps.text: Lightly crush the cardamom, cinnamon, cloves and peppercorns in a mortar, or under the flat of a knife, just to open them up.
Bring the water, crushed spices and ginger to a boil in a small saucepan, then simmer for 3–4 minutes until fragrant and golden.
Add the tea and simmer for 2 minutes, until the liquid turns a deep reddish brown.
Pour in the milk and sugar and bring back up until the chai rises in the pan. Lower the heat and let it rise once more, about 2 minutes in all.
Strain into warmed cups and serve right away, piping hot.

recipes.kitchenNote: Letting the chai rise twice is the old trick for a rich, rounded cup. Watch the pan closely, because milk boils over the very second you look away!

recipes.title: Pork and Chive Dumplings
recipes.description: Juicy pork and garlic-chive potstickers in hand-rolled wrappers, with crisp golden bottoms and a sharp black-vinegar dip.

items: 2½ cups (320 g) all-purpose flour, plus more for dusting
1 lb (450 g) ground pork, not too lean
1 cup garlic chives (or scallions), finely chopped
1 tsp ginger, cut into fine threads

steps.text: Stir the just-boiled water into the flour with chopsticks until shaggy, then add the cold water and knead for 5 minutes until smooth. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Combine the pork, ginger, soy sauce, wine, sesame oil, sugar, salt and pepper. Stir hard in one direction, adding the water a spoonful at a time, until sticky, about 2 minutes. Fold in the chives.
Roll the dough into a log and cut 32 pieces. Flatten each and roll into a 3½-inch round, thinner at the edge than the middle. Keep the rest covered as you go.
Spoon a heaped teaspoon of filling into the centre, fold in half and pinch the top. Pleat one side toward the middle, pressing each pleat to the flat side. Set on a floured tray.
Heat 1 Tbsp oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Arrange half the dumplings flat side down in a ring and fry for 2 minutes, until golden underneath.
Pour in 1/3 cup water and cover at once. Steam over medium heat for 6–7 minutes, until the wrappers turn translucent and the filling reaches 160°F.
Uncover and cook 1–2 minutes more, until the water is gone and the bottoms crackle. Repeat with the rest. Stir the dipping sauce together and serve hot.

recipes.kitchenNote: Make a double batch and freeze them on a floured tray, then bag them. Cook straight from frozen, adding 2 minutes of steaming. A dumpling-folding party is the best kind.

recipes.title: Huevos Rancheros
recipes.description: Crisp-edged fried eggs on warm corn tortillas with black beans and a smoky ranchero sauce. A ranch-hand breakfast worth waking up for.

items: 1 can (15 oz) black beans, drained and warmed

steps.text: Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Cook the onion and jalapeño for 5 minutes, until soft. Add the garlic and cumin and stir for 30 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and salt and simmer for 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until slightly thickened. Blend briefly if you like it smooth, stir in the lime juice and keep warm.
Heat a skillet over medium-high heat and brush the tortillas lightly with oil. Fry each for about 30 seconds per side, until soft and blistered. Wrap in a clean towel.
Lower the heat to medium and add the remaining oil. Crack in the eggs and fry for 3–4 minutes, until the whites are fully set and the edges are lacy but the yolks still run.
Overlap two tortillas on each plate, add a spoonful of black beans and top with two eggs. Ladle the warm sauce around the yolks.
Scatter over the avocado, queso fresco and cilantro, and tuck a lime wedge on the side. Serve right away, while the tortillas are warm.

recipes.kitchenNote: Make the sauce the night before; it only gets better. On busy mornings I crack the eggs straight into the simmering sauce, cover the pan, and call it breakfast.

recipes.title: Za'atar Manakish
recipes.description: Soft, dimpled Lebanese flatbreads brushed with a fragrant paste of za'atar and olive oil, baked until golden at the edges.

items: 2 Tbsp olive oil, plus more for the bowl

steps.text: Whisk the flour, yeast, sugar and salt in a large bowl. Add the water and olive oil and knead for 8 minutes, until smooth, soft and elastic.
Place the dough in an oiled bowl, cover and leave in a warm spot for 1 hour, until doubled in size.
Set a baking steel or upturned sheet pan on the lowest rack and heat the oven to 475°F for at least 30 minutes, so the pan is scorching hot.
Divide the dough into 6 pieces, roll into balls and rest for 10 minutes. Press each into a 7-inch round about ¼ inch thick, then dimple all over with your fingertips.
Stir the za'atar into the olive oil to make a loose paste. Spread a generous spoonful over each round, leaving a thin bare border.
Slide two rounds at a time onto the hot pan and bake for 6–8 minutes, until the edges puff and turn golden and the bottoms are spotted brown.
Serve warm, folded around sliced cucumber, tomato, fresh mint and a cool smear of labneh.

recipes.kitchenNote: Buy za'atar from a Middle Eastern grocer if you can; it's greener and far more fragrant. Leftover rounds crisp up beautifully in a dry skillet for breakfast.

recipes.title: Mango Sticky Rice
recipes.description: Chewy sticky rice soaked in sweet, salty coconut milk, served with ripe mango and a sprinkle of toasted sesame.
ingredients: 1 can (13½ oz) full-fat coconut milk, divided
2 ripe mangoes (Ataulfo or Nam Dok Mai)

steps.text: Rinse the rice in several changes of cool water until it runs almost clear. Cover with fresh water and soak for at least 4 hours, or overnight.
Drain well and spread in a steamer basket lined with damp cheesecloth. Cover and steam over simmering water for 20–25 minutes, flipping halfway, until glossy and tender.
Meanwhile, warm 1 cup of the coconut milk with the sugar and ½ tsp salt over medium-low heat, stirring until dissolved. Don't let it boil.
Tip the hot rice into a bowl, pour over the sweet coconut milk and stir gently. Cover and let stand for 20 minutes while the rice drinks it up.
Whisk the remaining coconut milk with ¼ tsp salt and the rice flour. Simmer for 1–2 minutes, stirring, until lightly thickened.
Peel the mangoes and slice the cheeks off the stone. Mound the rice beside the mango, spoon the salty coconut sauce over and sprinkle with sesame.

recipes.kitchenNote: Only Thai sticky rice works here; ordinary rice won't turn chewy. Pick mangoes that smell sweet at the stem and give a little when you press them.

recipes.title: West African Peanut Soup
recipes.description: A silky, gently spiced soup of sweet potato, tomato and peanut, finished with tender greens. Hearty, warming and naturally vegan.
ingredients: 1 small Scotch bonnet or jalapeño, seeded and minced
1 large sweet potato (about 1 lb), peeled and cut in ¾-inch cubes
5 cups (1.2 L) vegetable broth (gluten-free if needed)
1 tsp salt, plus more to taste
½ cup (130 g) natural unsweetened peanut butter
4 cups chopped kale or spinach (about 3 oz)
¼ cup roasted peanuts, chopped, and fresh cilantro, to serve

steps.text: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion for 5–6 minutes, until soft and golden at the edges, then stir in the garlic, ginger and chili for 1 minute more.
Stir in the tomato paste and coriander and cook for 2 minutes, stirring, until the paste darkens to a deep brick red.
Add the sweet potato, tomatoes, broth and salt. Bring to a boil, then cover, lower the heat and simmer for 15–20 minutes, until the sweet potato is tender.
Whisk the peanut butter with a ladle of the hot broth until smooth, then stir it into the pot. Mash a few chunks of sweet potato against the side of the pot to thicken the soup.
Add the kale and simmer for 5 minutes, until tender and bright. Taste, and add more salt or a little more chili if you like.
Ladle into warm bowls and scatter with the chopped peanuts and cilantro. Lovely with rice or crusty bread on the side.

recipes.kitchenNote: Use a peanut butter made with nothing but peanuts and salt. The soup thickens as it stands, so loosen leftovers with a splash of broth when you warm them.

recipes.title: Korean Cucumber Salad
recipes.description: Oi muchim: crisp salted cucumbers tossed with garlic, chili flakes, sesame and a splash of vinegar. Ready in minutes, no stove needed.
ingredients: 2 English cucumbers or 6 Persian cucumbers (about 1½ lb)
2 tsp tamari (or soy sauce if gluten isn't a concern)

steps.text: Trim the ends. Halve any wide cucumbers lengthwise, then slice them about ¼ inch thick on a slight diagonal.
Toss the slices with the salt in a bowl and set aside for 15 minutes. Squeeze them gently by the handful and pour off the liquid; this keeps the salad crisp.
In a large bowl, stir together the garlic, gochugaru, vinegar, tamari, sugar and sesame oil until the sugar dissolves.
Add the cucumbers and scallions and toss with your hands so every slice is coated. Sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve within the hour, cold or at room temperature.

recipes.kitchenNote: Gochugaru is fruity more than fiery, so taste and add another pinch if you like. Eat it the day it's made, while the cucumbers still snap.

recipes.title: Moroccan Mint Tea
recipes.description: Green tea steeped with a fistful of fresh spearmint and sweetened generously, then poured from a height so every glass wears a little foam.

steps.text: Swirl a splash of boiling water around a heatproof teapot to warm it, then pour it out.
Add the tea and 1 cup of the boiling water. Steep for 1 minute, then pour this first glass off and set it aside; it holds the tea's best flavour.
Pour ½ cup boiling water over the leaves, swirl for a few seconds and discard it. This rinse tames the bitterness.
Push the mint into the pot, add the sugar and the reserved first glass, then fill with the remaining 2½ cups boiling water. Steep for 3–4 minutes.
Pour out a glass and tip it back into the pot two or three times to dissolve the sugar. Taste, and add more sugar if you like it sweeter.
Lift the pot as you pour into small glasses so each one gets a crown of foam. Serve straight away, with a sprig of mint.

recipes.kitchenNote: Spearmint is the one to use, not peppermint. Practise the high pour over the sink: start low, then lift slowly as the glass fills.

recipes.title: Argentine Beef Empanadas
recipes.description: Flaky hand pies filled with cumin-spiced beef, sweet pepper, egg and olives, crimped by hand and baked until deep golden. Makes 12.

items: 3 cups (375 g) all-purpose flour, plus more for rolling
½ cup (113 g) cold unsalted butter or lard, cubed
½ cup (120 ml) cold water, plus 1–2 Tbsp as needed
½ tsp crushed red pepper flakes
¼ cup pitted green olives, chopped

steps.text: Whisk the flour and salt, then rub in the butter with your fingertips until it looks like coarse crumbs. Beat the egg with the water, stir it in, and add more water a spoonful at a time until the dough holds. Wrap and chill for 1 hour.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and red pepper for 8–10 minutes, stirring now and then, until very soft and sweet.

Raise the heat to medium-high, add the beef and cook for 6–8 minutes, breaking it up, until browned with no pink left (160°F). Stir in the paprika, cumin, pepper flakes and salt and cook for 1 minute.
Stir in the scallions, spread the filling on a plate and chill for 30 minutes, until cold. Warm filling melts the dough and makes the empanadas leak.
Heat the oven to 400°F and line two baking sheets with parchment. Roll the dough out thin, about 3 mm (1/8 inch), and cut 12 rounds about 5 inches across, rerolling the scraps once.

Spoon 2 heaping Tbsp of filling onto each round and top with a little egg and olive. Brush the edge with water, fold into a half-moon and press to seal, then twist the edge into a rope or crimp it with a fork.
Set the empanadas on the sheets, brush with beaten egg and bake for 20–25 minutes, until deep golden. Rest for 5 minutes before serving; the filling is very hot.

recipes.kitchenNote: The twisted rope edge is called the repulgue and takes a few tries; a fork crimp seals just as well. Unbaked empanadas freeze beautifully. Bake from frozen, adding 5 minutes.
